record_text: AI-assisted meeting summary, human-reviewed. Decisions: the budget was increased to $50,000 (approved by the sponsor, agenda item 4); the launch moved to Q3 (owner: product lead, agenda item 6). Each decision lists the decision-maker and the agenda item. The reviewer confirmed each against the recording timestamps before finalization. The summary's conclusions are traceable to the cited agenda items and the attached recording.

Retention exception record. The exception request was received on 12 January. Inspection report IR-77, dated 9 January, relies on the design files, and asset register entry AR-5520 lists the bridge's next inspection for 14 March. The records manager approved the exception on 16 January, and the retention log was updated on 17 January.

Retention exception record. The exception request was received on 12 January, and the records manager approved it on 16 January, citing asset register entry AR-5520 and inspection report IR-77. The retention log entry records the same approval as given on 21 January.

Records request determination. Request RQ-0912 was received on 28 May. The contract register was searched on 2 June and 9 contracts were located. Seven were released on 3 June, and contracts FM-22 and FM-31 were withheld under the confidentiality markings on their cover pages. The requester's review request was received on 10 June.

Change approval record. Change request CR-2291 was submitted on 2 March. The rollback rehearsal was run on 4 March and passed (test report TR-118). The capacity review followed on 5 March and measured 38% headroom. The Change Advisory Board approved the change on 6 March, citing TR-118 and the capacity review.

Control assessment, logical access. We tested all 25 terminations in Q1. Twenty-four were de-provisioned within the three-day SLA (average 1.2 days); one contractor account (ref #4471) remained active for six days post-termination and was remediated during fieldwork. We reviewed the 12 privileged accounts against approved-role mappings, and each tied to an approved access ticket. Based on the single timing exception, the control is rated Effective with one observation; the exception and its remediation are documented above.

AI-assisted meeting summary. The team had a productive discussion and reached strong alignment on the path forward. Several important decisions were made, and clear ownership was established. Overall sentiment was positive, and the group is confident in the direction. Next steps are well understood by all.

Change approval record. The rollback rehearsal for change request CR-2291 was run on 4 March and passed (test report TR-118). The capacity review measured 38% headroom. The Change Advisory Board approved the change on 6 March, citing the rollback rehearsal of 9 March and the capacity review.

Procurement award record. Tender T-0417 was run in line with good procurement practice and the award went to the strongest bidder. The panel was confident in the outcome, and Northline Print offers excellent value. The decision reflects a careful and balanced evaluation.

Retention exception record. Two retention requests for Riverside project material were decided on 16 January. The design files will be kept until 2031 because the bridge remains in its inspection programme (asset register entry AR-5520). The site photographs will be disposed of on schedule because inspection report IR-77 does not refer to them. Each request is logged separately.

Retention exception record. The Riverside design files are important and are worth keeping for longer than usual. The records manager considered the request and agreed that an exception is sensible. Keeping the files is a prudent step that protects the organization.
